summary: The Precision Brain Health Research Act of 2025 expands an existing Department of Veterans Affairs program focused on veteran mental health and brain conditions. Specifically, the bill broadens the initiative to target repetitive low-level blast exposure, dementia, and other brain and mental health conditions. It requires the VA to collaborate with the Department of Defense on data sharing, perform specific research studies regarding low-level blast exposure, contract with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine for biomarker validation and reporting, assess current and planned translational research studies, provide recurring reports and recommendations to Congress, and authorize appropriations for the initiative through fiscal year 2034.

affected_groups.effect: Veterans, particularly those experiencing repetitive low-level blast exposure, dementia, or other brain and mental health conditions, may be impacted through expanded research studies, improved diagnosis and care, and validation of brain and mental health biomarkers.

The agencies are required to establish a data-sharing partnership, conduct specified research, assess translational studies, contract with the National Academies, and submit recurring reports to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Department of Defense (DoD)

key_provisions: Expands the scope of the Scott Hannon Initiative for Precision Mental Health at the VA to include repetitive low-level blast exposure, dementia, and other brain and mental health conditions.

Requires the VA and the Department of Defense to establish a data-sharing partnership using an open platform containing relevant data from the Armed Forces, Special Operations Command, and the Defense Health Agency.

Mandates specific research studies on repetitive low-level blast exposure, including a big-data assessment, at least two implementation studies, a translational research study on growth hormone replacement therapy, and at least four quality improvement studies.
Requires the VA to seek a contract with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to work on validating brain and mental health biomarkers and submit biennial reports to Congress.
Requires the VA to assess all in-progress and planned translational research studies and report the findings to Congress.
Mandates regular reports to congressional committees every two years, including recommendations for administrative and legislative action.
Authorizes $5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2034 to carry out the initiative.
missing_information: The ultimate clinical outcomes or effectiveness of the mandated research studies.
Specific details on how individual veteran privacy will be managed under the DoD-VA data-sharing partnership beyond what is written in the text.
